data.description:

The latest La Colorada vein update slots directly into one of the main catalysts in the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St, which highlights expanding inferred resources and new structures such as Elena and Filomena as a support for future mine inventory. Fresh drill intercepts and channel samples from Elena, Denisse, Catalina and Filomena plus La Chona Breccia give that storyline more technical detail.

Execution risk sits around integrating these zones, maintaining metallurgical performance in line with testing, and doing so while gold operations, Jacobina remediation and large capex at La Colorada Skarn and Timmins are all competing for capital and management focus.

data.title: Don't Ignore The Insider Selling In Piper Sandler Companies
data.description:
We wouldn't blame Piper Sandler Companies (NYSE:PIPR) shareholders if they were a little worried about the fact that Jonathan Doyle, the Senior Managing Principal recently netted about US$939k selling shares at an average price of US$62.63. However, it's crucial to note that they remain very much invested in the stock and that sale only reduced their holding by 3.1%.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Piper Sandler Companies Insider Transactions Over The Last Year

Notably, that recent sale by Senior Managing Principal Jonathan Doyle was not the only time they sold Piper Sandler Companies shares this year. They previously made an even bigger sale of -US$7.1m worth of shares at a price of US$81.08 per share. We generally don't like to see insider selling, but the lower the sale price, the more it concerns us. The silver lining is that this sell-down took place above the latest price (US$62.68). So it may not shed much light on insider confidence at current levels.

Jonathan Doyle ditched 105.00k shares over the year. The average price per share was US$76.53. Insider Ownership Of Piper Sandler Companies

Many investors like to check how much of a company is owned by insiders. We usually like to see fairly high levels of insider ownership. It's great to see that Piper Sandler Companies insiders own 3.3% of the company, worth about US$140m. Most shareholders would be happy to see this sort of insider ownership, since it suggests that management incentives are well aligned with other shareholders.

What Might The Insider Transactions At Piper Sandler Companies Tell Us?

An insider sold Piper Sandler Companies shares recently, but they didn't buy any. And even if we look at the last year, we didn't see any purchases. But since Piper Sandler Companies is profitable and growing, we're not too worried by this. It is good to see high insider ownership, but the insider selling leaves us cautious.
